summary: Gave the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission more time to finish its work, extending its deadline to September 2, 1908.

Guaranteed a jury trial in Canal Zone criminal cases punishable by death or life imprisonment, setting up jury commissions to draw 60 qualified male residents per term and listing who is exempt from service.
Created Jewel Cave National Monument inside the Black Hills National Forest, protecting the cave as a formation of scientific interest; the monument takes priority, though forest uses may continue.
Allowed S. Baillio to be reinstated at the Norfolk Navy Yard regardless of how long he had been out of service.
Permitted Douglas B. Thompson, who left Isthmus of Panama service because of illness, to be reinstated with the option of transfer to a department that wants to hire him despite his disability.
Reserved specified lands in Washington for lighthouse purposes.
Enlarged the Modoc National Forest in California by adding nearby lands that are partly timbered.
Amended civil-service Rule III so messengers in the Office of Indian Affairs can be among the Indians given noncompetitive examinations for appointment.
Abolished the Yellowstone Land District in Montana and moved its lands to the Glasgow Land District.
Abolished the North Platte Land District in Nebraska and shifted its lands to the Alliance Land District.
Amended Executive Order 746, which merged the Woodward and Alva land districts, to place the combined land office at Woodward, Oklahoma.

Set a strict procedure for recommending changes in how classified positions are filled: each needs a full statement of reasons, department-head approval and a Civil Service Commission report to the President.
Amended Executive Order 755 to move additional Montana lands from the old Yellowstone Land District into the Glasgow Land District.
Reserved land at Lowell Point on Resurrection Bay, Alaska, for the Navy Department as a coaling depot.
Allowed Edwyn N. Purvis, formerly of the Isthmian Canal Service, to be appointed a clerk in the classified service in the United States without civil-service rules.
Permitted Edward J. Tupper's appointment as deputy collector and inspector of customs at Stamford, Connecticut, without following the civil-service rules.

Set aside the small mangrove and salt-grass islets, shoals and sand bars of Mosquito Inlet and the Halifax and Hillsboro river mouths as the Mosquito Inlet Reservation, a preserve and breeding ground for native birds.
Authorized building fortifications on Corregidor Island in Manila Bay, Philippines, once any needed lands are secured.
Moved Mississippi from the Louisiana internal revenue collection district to the Alabama district.
Shrank the Lincoln National Forest in New Mexico by redrawing its boundaries and returning excluded lands to the public domain. (The Statutes' contents table misprints "Monument" for "Forest.")
Reserved a square tract of public land at Hogan, Alaska, as a military reservation for the Army Signal Corps to run telegraph lines.
Allowed Charles L. Babcock to be appointed an immigrant inspector for confidential duty in the Immigration Service without a civil-service examination.
Revoked the executive order of March 26, 1901, and prescribed a new ration for the Army.
Created the Ozark National Forest from partly timbered public lands in Arkansas, reserving them from settlement or entry for the use and benefit of the people.
Moved Philip W. Reinhard Jr., confidential clerk to the New York collector of customs, from the excepted to the competitive class in recognition of nine years of faithful service.
Reserved lands near Chena and Fairbanks, Alaska, for Army Signal Corps telegraph lines and revoked Executive Order 328-B.
Added caretakers of abandoned military reservations or posts to the positions excepted from examination, when the jobs go to retired noncommissioned officers or enlisted men.
Reserved part of Hawkins Island in Prince William Sound, Alaska, as a Navy coaling station.
Allowed Wilhelm Lutz, assistant chief of police of Porto Rico, to be appointed to the U.S. Immigration Bureau for reasons given by Governor Post.
Redrew the Navy coaling-depot reservation at Lowell Point on Resurrection Bay, Alaska, about 3,350 acres including Tonsina Creek waters, and revoked the earlier Executive Order 760.
Tweaked the Canal Zone jury-trial order (Executive Order 750) by replacing "collector of revenue" with "tax collector" on the jury commissions.
Revoked an executive order of May 9, 1898, that had reserved lands in Washington.
Confirmed Executive Order 707, which reinstated John P. Scruggs.

Made four hours a full Saturday's work at overseas naval stations during set hot months, from Cavite and Olongapo to Guam, Tutuila, Honolulu, Guantanamo and San Juan, with time-and-a-half for extra hours.
Transferred a parcel in Sitka, Alaska, from the Navy Department to the Army Signal Corps as a site for a cable house and station for military cable and telegraph lines.
Excused classified employees who lost their health while saving life in the line of duty from examination and reinstatement requirements.
Reserved all the Dry Tortugas islands as the Tortugas Keys Reservation, a preserve and breeding ground for native birds; military use may continue except on Bird Key.
Allowed Harry A. Strohm, an Indiana third-class postmaster with nine years' experience, to be appointed a special agent in the Third Assistant Postmaster-General's office without examination.
Permitted Henry C. Towers, a Bureau of Forestry expert, to be promoted to expert and chief of the section of purchases without examination.
Redrew the Manzano National Forest in New Mexico, folding in the Mount Taylor National Forest, adding timbered lands and returning excluded lands to the public domain.
Created Natural Bridges National Monument in Utah's San Juan County, protecting the Augusta, Caroline and Little bridges on White Canyon with 40 acres around each.
Reserved a tract on the Chena River at Fairbanks, Alaska, as a military reservation for an Army Signal Corps wireless telegraph station.
Allowed William S. Murphy of Mississippi, valued for his legal training, to be appointed a Chinese inspector in the Immigration Service without examination.
Redrew the Sierra National Forest, adding partly timbered lands in California and Nevada and excluding some California lands.
Allowed Alpheus H. Mahone to be reinstated as a fish culturist in the Bureau of Fisheries despite the civil-service time limit.
Excepted up to 20 special agents in the Interstate Commerce Commission's division of prosecutions from examination, with the Civil Service Commission able to revoke the privilege if abused.
Allowed John Krey to be reinstated as an assistant engineer in the Army's Engineer Department without regard to the civil-service time limit.
Enlarged the Jemez National Forest in New Mexico with additional partly timbered lands.
Reduced the San Juan National Forest in Colorado.
Rewrote a Canal Zone law to make it a misdemeanor to willfully damage, deface or remove boundary or survey monuments and signals.
Gave federal employees in San Francisco, Oakland, Berkeley and Alameda May 6, 1908, off for the reception of the battleship fleet.
Enlarged the Camp Stotsenburg military reservation near Angeles, Pampanga, on Luzon in the Philippines.
Allowed Katherine J. Fenton to be appointed a copyist draftsman in the Washington departments without civil-service rules.
Reserved fourteen tracts in Alaska, mostly along the Yukon River, as military reservations for stations on the Third Section of the U.S. Military Telegraph Lines.
Removed lands in California from a lighthouse reserve created by an executive order of January 26, 1867.
Created Lewis and Clark Cavern National Monument, protecting a limestone cavern near Limespur in Jefferson County, Montana, with 160 acres around its entrance.

summary: Created a commission, chaired by Capt. Adolph Marx, to review U.S. laws on the safety of passengers and crews aboard American vessels and recommend revisions.
Directed department heads to align salaries with the Committee on Grades and Salaries' recommendations, paying similar salaries for similar work as far as practicable.
Reserved public lands on Biliran Island in the Philippines for military purposes.
Renamed the Garden City National Forest the Kansas National Forest and enlarged it with lands partly covered by timber or undergrowth.
Reserved a small tract at Chena, Alaska, as a military reservation for Army Signal Corps telegraph operations.
Redrew the Dixie National Forest, adding partly timbered lands in Arizona and excluding some lands in Utah.
Allowed Richard H. Taylor of California to stay on as an immigrant inspector handling confidential investigations for as long as the Department of Commerce and Labor needs him.
Excused Civil War and Spanish War veterans in government service on May 27, 1908, for a parade marking the removal of Vice President George Clinton's body.
Allowed the Interstate Commerce Commission to employ John M. Jones as a tariff and traffic expert without examination, at the Commission's discretion.
Enlarged the Pocatello National Forest in Idaho and Utah by adding the Port Neuf National Forest and part of the Bear River National Forest.
Renamed part of the Bear River National Forest the Cache National Forest from July 1, 1908, with the rest joining the Pocatello National Forest; no land was added or released.
Abolished the Fort Keough military reservation and turned it over to the Interior Department.
Extended Executive Order 795's salary-alignment rules to clerks and draftsmen at navy yards.
Allowed the Interstate Commerce Commission to employ Charles Lutz in charge of statistics and accounts without examination, at the Commission's discretion.
Authorized disposal of the former Pennsylvania Railroad Company station in Washington.
Set a four-hour Saturday workday from July through September for skilled mechanics at navy yards.
Reserved portions of Man Key and Woman Key, Florida, for the Navy Department.
Directed executive departments and bureaus to gather and furnish data requested by the new National Conservation Commission on the condition and needs of the nation's natural resources.
Redrew the boundaries of the Lemmon Land District in North and South Dakota.
Revoked Executive Orders 447 and 584.
Allowed William J. Dow to be reinstated at the Government Printing Office as private secretary to the Public Printer despite the civil-service time limit.
Set the salary of Immigration Commission member William R. Wheeler at $7,500 a year.
Created the Whitman National Forest in Oregon.
Created the Malheur National Forest in Oregon.
Created the Umatilla National Forest in Oregon.
Created the Deschutes National Forest in Oregon.
Created the Fremont National Forest in Oregon.
Reserved all unpatented public lands within 60 feet of the Canadian border, putting the strip under federal control to better enforce customs and immigration laws; only public highways are allowed.
Waived civil-service temporary-appointment rules so the Treasury Secretary could staff up to carry out the 1908 act amending the national banking laws.
Allowed former classified employee Andrew Christensen to be appointed a General Land Office special agent despite reinstatement and transfer limits.
Redrew the Gila National Forest in New Mexico, absorbing the Big Burros National Forest and new lands, while the rest of the old Gila became part of the Datil National Forest.
Established the Datil National Forest in New Mexico from part of the Gila National Forest plus additional partly timbered lands.
Allowed retired commissary sergeant John McCarthy to be appointed without examination as laborer in charge of a Subsistence Department warehouse in New York, given his unusual experience.
Renamed part of the Rainier National Forest the Columbia National Forest from July 1, 1908, without adding or releasing any land.
Changed the Rainier National Forest in Washington.
Reduced the Washington National Forest in Washington.
Established the Chelan National Forest in Washington.
Established the Snoqualmie National Forest in Washington.
Established the Wenatchee National Forest in Washington.
